ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 6, in the circuit, R1 and R2 are both variable resistors, the internal resistance of the power supply cannot be ignored, and the plates of the parallel-plate capacitor C are placed horizontally. Close switch S, and when the circuit reaches stability, the charged oil droplet is suspended between the two plates and remains motionless. If only one of the following conditions is changed, the one under which the oil droplet can still remain motionless is (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Increase the resistance value of R2

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 6, in the circuit, R1 and R2 are both variable resistors, the internal resistance of the power supply cannot be ignored, and the plates of the parallel-plate capacitor C are placed horizontally. Close switch S, and when the circuit reaches stability, the charged oil droplet is suspended between the two plates and remains motionless. If only one condition is allowed to be changed, what adjustment should be made so that the oil droplet can still remain motionless?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Increase the resistance value of R2
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the power supply E with internal resistance r and switch S; in the middle there is a vertical branch, with R1 connected between the upper and lower main nodes; above, from the upper main node to the right, variable resistor R2 is connected in series, and then connected to the upper plate of the parallel-plate capacitor C on the right side; the lower plate of the capacitor is connected back to the lower main node. The two plates of the capacitor are placed horizontally, and a charged oil droplet is drawn between the plates. Then reason: After S is closed and DC stability is reached, no DC current passes through the capacitor branch, so there is no steady current in R2, which is in series with the capacitor, and there is no voltage drop across R2. Therefore, the voltage across capacitor C is equal to the terminal voltage between the upper and lower main nodes. This terminal voltage is determined by the power supply E, the internal resistance r, and the parallel load R1, and is not determined by R2. For the oil droplet to remain motionless, the electric field force must balance gravity, that is, qU_C/d = mg; if the plate spacing d does not change and U_C does not change, then the oil droplet still remains motionless. When only the resistance value of R2 is changed, the stable U_C remains unchanged, so R2 can be adjusted. According to the requirement of the problem, the resistance value of R2 should be increased.
